title: Stream session recovery pipeline deadtime — postmortem and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

On 2026-04-11 between 02:37 and 03:18 UTC we observed a severe degradation of hosted-API streaming sessions: sustained TTFB p95 jump from ~120ms to ~2.3s, large increase in streaming reconnects and ~18% request-level 5xx rate for streaming routes. Customer-visible symptoms included choppy streaming responses, long initial delays for early tokens, and client reconnect storms. Total impact window ~41 minutes, estimated 14k affected streaming sessions (global customers). No data exfiltration; model outputs were delayed rather than incorrect.

Severity: P0.

Primary impact: streaming-mode requests on hosted API experienced high initial latency and session fragmentation; synchronous generation endpoints were mostly unaffected.

Detection and alerting timeline:
- 02:37 UTC: synthetic streaming TTFB p95 started to rise (automated sliding-window anomaly triggered internally but routed to the telemetry queue due to high load).
- 02:41 UTC: edge layer reports increased acceptor queue lengths in ap-south1 region.
- 02:45 UTC: first on-call notification — SRE rotation alerted to streaming-p95 spike.
- 02:51 UTC: paging escalation to SRE lead after client support tickets spike.
- 03:06 UTC: initial mitigation (increase acceptor consumer tasks, disable a recently-deployed coalescing change) applied as hotfix; partial improvement.
- 03:18 UTC: traffic returned to baseline after dynamic backpressure thresholds and KV lease refresh patch rolled out cluster-wide. Post-incident monitoring verified stable signal.

Root cause (summary):
A confluence of three factors created a transient deadtime in the streaming session recovery pipeline:
1) Scheduler coalescing change (deployed 2026-04-09) that grouped small acceptor wakeups into larger intervals to save CPU. Under certain burst patterns this increased worst-case scheduling jitter.
2) An acceptor-side backoff/hedge loop had a regression that extended its exponential backoff floor when a specific edge keepalive pattern was seen, delaying session rehydration attempts by an order of magnitude.
3) A KV-lease refresh race between the acceptor pool and the midchain cache resulted in temporary stale KV entries for session metadata; stale metadata meant reconnect attempts could not find active prefixes, causing client retries and upstream fanout amplification.

Combined effect: scheduler jitter + extended backoff produced a ~1.6–2.2s window where many session rebinds were delayed. During that window reconnects and hedges amplified load on acceptor queues, which then hit the coalesced scheduler's worst-case path causing additional latency — a positive feedback loop.

Why existing alerts were insufficient:
- We monitor p99 and absolute queue-depth thresholds; this issue exhibited a fast-moving p95 slope and short-lived spikes which didn’t cross p99 or static queue thresholds consistently.
- The synthetic check that could have predicted the cascading behavior was enqueued behind the same telemetry pipeline that experienced queueing delay, so its alert arrived late.

Root cause evidence (artifacts):
- acceptor service logs show clustered "session-rebind delayed" entries starting 02:36:58 UTC.
- midchain KV metrics show a sharp increase in stale-lease hits from 02:38:12–02:39:24 UTC.
- profiler traces captured scheduler wakeup gaps at 02:37:04–02:39:00 UTC with >1.1s gaps between wakeups on affected hosts.

Immediate mitigations performed during incident:
1) Scaled acceptor worker pool by +40% (03:06 UTC) to increase rehydration throughput.
2) Rolled back the scheduler coalescing flag in the acceptor fleet (03:08 UTC), restoring the previous wakeup granularity.
3) Applied an emergency hotfix to the backoff loop to cap the minimum backoff at 100ms under any keepalive pattern (03:12 UTC).
4) Forced KV-lease refresh for midchain caches (03:14 UTC) using an orchestrated refresh command.

These mitigations cumulatively reduced the feedback amplification and restored normal session recovery times by ~03:18 UTC.

Why the mitigations worked:
- Rolling back coalescing removed scheduling jitter that lengthened recovery windows.
- Capping the backoff reduced per-session rebind delay and smoothed retry traffic.
- Forcing lease refresh removed the stale-metadata failure mode so reconnects succeeded once scheduled.

Customer impact estimates and telemetry:
- Affected streaming sessions: ~14k (based on reconnect/close pairs during window).
- Error budget blow: estimated 0.9% increase for streaming SLA in the rolling 1-hour window.
- Top regions: us-west1, eu-west1 experienced most client reconnects; ap-south1 earlier had acceptor queue growth.

Post-incident analysis and corrective actions (short-term):
- ACTION 1 (SRE): Add a sliding-window p95 slope alert to streaming TTFB (owner: Markus Chen, due: 2026-04-20).
- ACTION 2 (Serving Runtime): Revert coalescing change permanently unless re-introduced with safety gating and load-simulation (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-04-25).
- ACTION 3 (Eng infra): Add priority path for telemetry/synthetic alerting that cannot be backpressured by normal runtime metrics (owner: Kim Nguyen, due: 2026-04-22).
- ACTION 4 (Serving Runtime): Patch acceptor backoff logic to include a safety cap and add unit/integration tests for keepalive patterns (owner: Sophie Ramirez, due: 2026-04-28).
- ACTION 5 (SRE + Runtime): Implement proactive KV-lease health metric (stale-lease-rate) and alert when crossing 0.5% baseline (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-04-21).

Long-term engineering changes (investigations and roadmap items):
- Replace coarse scheduler coalescing with adaptive coalescing that observes tail latency and disables itself under bursty workloads.
- Improve session-rehydration state machine to tolerate transient stale metadata by adding a short local cache read-through before declaring miss.
- Model a synthetic load test that replays the observed keepalive pattern and reconnect storm to verify safety of future optimizations.
- Add a run-level circuit breaker that can isolate the acceptor sub-pool and progressively drain/restore rather than cluster-wide rollback.

Runbook draft (for on-call SRE) — immediate triage steps for a similar event:
1) Verify streaming-ttfb p95, p90, and p95-slope graphs in the streaming dashboard.
2) Check acceptor queue depth by region and list top 5 hosts with highest backlog.
3) If backlog rising and p95 slope > 200ms/min, scale acceptor workers by +30% in affected pool.
4) Inspect acceptor service flags: if "scheduler-coalesce" is true, flip to false for affected pool and observe wakeup latency within 90s.
5) Run midchain KV-lease health check: if stale-lease-rate > 0.5%, trigger manual refresh command (sre-tools midchain refresh --region <r>).
6) If reconnect/hedge traffic continues to amplify, apply backoff floor override (acceptor flag: backoff-min-ms=100).
7) If mitigation fails after 10 minutes, fail traffic to dedicated fallback route (route: hosted-stream-fallback-dedicated) to protect control plane.
8) Open an incident thread, annotate timeline, and collect sample logs from top 5 acceptor hosts.

Operational notes:
- Keep the emergency backoff-floor until the long-term fix lands and has been validated in canary.
- Do not use standard p99 alerts alone to triage streaming incidents; p95 slope is now a primary signal for this class of failure.

Postmortem review notes and open questions: 
- Was the scheduler coalescing rollout missing synthetic load gating? Evidence suggests the rollout used unit and low-traffic canaries only. Need process fix.
- Why did the telemetry queue allow synthetic alert delay? Evaluate separate priority lanes for synthetic checks.
- Can we instrument the rebind path to calculate end-to-end time from client reconnect to session rehydration for better SLOs?

Appendix (observability pointers and commands):
- dashboards: Streaming > TTFB (global) | Acceptors > queue-depth-by-host | Midchain > stale-lease-rate.
- useful logs: acceptor-service: /var/log/acceptor/wakeup.log ; midchain: /var/log/midchain/lease.log.
- quick commands: sre-tools acceptor-scale --pool streaming--ap-south1 +40 ; sre-tools midchain refresh --all-affected ; curl -H 'X-Trace' https://internal-api/acceptor/health

Follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-04-19 15:00 UTC (SRE + serving-runtime + infra) to review progress on ACTION items and sign off on runbook changes.
